title: Third Law of Black Hole Mechanics Proven for BTZ Black Holes
excerpt: Researchers have proven that a Third Law of black hole mechanics holds for the BTZ black hole in three-dimensional gravity, while demonstrating that scalar field collapse can still form an extremal
content:
A theoretical physics study published in the Journal of High Energy Physics proves that a Third Law of black hole mechanics holds for the BTZ black hole in three-dimensional gravity coupled to matter obeying the dominant energy condition. Conducted by researchers Aidan M. McSharry, Harvey S. Reall, and Jorge E. Santos, the research addresses fundamental mechanical bounds governing black hole evolution in three dimensions.

According to the proven Third Law, initial data containing a trapped surface cannot evolve in finite time to a black hole that coincides with extremal BTZ on the event horizon. The authors established that this limitation holds firmly for any choice of boundary conditions at infinity, demonstrating a strict constraint on the dynamical evolution of these horizons.

The mathematical proof relies on defining a quasilocal energy and angular momentum within the three-dimensional gravitational theory. Using spinorial methods, the authors established a BPS inequality that is saturated by the extremal BTZ solution, thereby providing the analytical foundation that prevents finite-time evolution from initial trapped surfaces to the extremal horizon.

Despite this general prohibition for trapped surfaces, the study demonstrates that gravitational collapse of a massless scalar field can nevertheless result in the formation of an extremal BTZ black hole in finite time. The authors explain that the difference between these two contrasting outcomes arises because gravitational collapse occurs in the Neveu-Schwarz sector, whereas the extremal BTZ black hole is supersymmetric in the Ramond sector.

Finally, the authors discuss gravitational solutions that settle down to extremal BTZ in infinite time along the event horizon. Together, these theoretical findings map out the boundaries between forbidden and permissible pathways toward extremal BTZ black hole configurations in three-dimensional gravity coupled to matter.
